segments.line: At the city gate, a dozen soldiers point their spears at you. You
honk the horn.
Every single one of them drops his spear and hits the ground.
Mo laughs so hard he cries.
They decide you must be gods. Or at least friends of the gods. Nobody wants to find out which. Then there's a problem nobody saw coming.
Julius Caesar banned carts from the streets of Rome during the day, because the traffic was so bad. That's real. An
official runs after you, waving a wax tablet.
Is a cart with no horse still a cart? Nobody knows. So nobody stops you. You
roll through the Forum at walking speed. Thousands of people follow you. Mo
plugs in his phone and turns the music all the way up. A crowd of Romans tries to dance to it. Badly. A
senator offers you a bag of gold coins for a ride around the block. You
take him. Then five more.
Kids run alongside the car all the way down the street. You
show them the windshield wipers. They think it's magic.
Honestly, so does Mo. At
night, Rome goes completely dark. No streetlights. Just torches and the moon. Then
you switch on your headlights. For one second, the whole street is silent. Then
a thousand people scream. And then
the big one. The Circus Maximus, the chariot track.
Up to a hundred and fifty thousand people in the stands. That's real. The
best charioteer in Rome challenges you to a race.
Four horses, against a hundred and fifty under the hood. You
let him lead for one lap. Just to be polite. Then
you put your foot down. You
win by three laps. The crowd goes insane. Mo
stands up through the sunroof with his arms in the air. 'We're legends! ' Then you
look at the fuel gauge. It's already at half.
